title: Check failures: show the failing tests to the fix round and run a failed check once more before sending it
lead: *Proposed.* When the project check command fails, ork runs it once more before it starts a fix round. If the rerun passes, the round is not spent and the run record says the check was flaky. If it fails again, the fix-round brief starts with the failing test names and their assertion lines (bounded), then the output tail as before.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
Observed on S207's fix round (wave 4, 2026-11-02, `.scratch/v11/wave4-friction.md`, F23 to F25). Anchors re-checked against main on 2026-11-07 (after S294, S235 and S238 landed).

1. The excerpt had no failing assertion (F23). Verified in code: a red check goes to `bumpRound` with the log as feedback (`internal/engine/states.go:231-232`). The brief for it is the last 30000 bytes of the log (`states.go:110-111`), and the log holds the last 30000 bytes of the command's stdout plus stderr, then `slicer check --json` (`states.go:294`, `:306`). There is no step that looks for `--- FAIL` lines. So a header and assertion that sit earlier than the last 30000 bytes of output (for example before a race report or a timeout panic with its goroutine dump) are dropped. The landing re-check brief does the same (`internal/engine/land.go:179`). *Not verified:* what the S207 log held, because run logs live in `~/.local/state/ork/runs/` (outside this workspace, not read). The implementer's own words (it could not see the failing assertion, so it asked whether the fix round may edit the TUI and daemon files S207 excludes) are the only evidence of what the brief showed.
2. The failure did not reproduce (F24). The orchestrator ran the two packages alone in the S207 worktree, and both passed: without `-race` `internal/daemon` 47.0s and `internal/tui` 3.8s (`.scratch/v11/s207-dt.out`), with `-race` 78.2s and 39.9s (`.scratch/v11/s207-dt-race.out`). The code runs the check once and treats a red result as final (`runChecks`, `states.go:268-327`). `RunCheck` knows only OK or not (`internal/engine/check.go:19-34`, `CheckOutput` at `internal/engine/engine.go:28-31`), so a timeout and an exit failure look the same to `runChecks`. Each wasted fix round also spends one of the run's implementer rounds. Since S294 the limit pauses rather than stops: `bumpRound` (`states.go:157-189`) pauses for the owner (pending kind `rounds`) after round `DefaultPauseRound`, 3 (`internal/engine/engine.go:25`), or at once when `noProgress` (`states.go:136-153`) sees the same implementer tree and the same check log hash in two adjacent rounds.
3. Load (F25). Verified: a run counts against the global cap (default 2, adj 172) while its engine goroutine is busy, and that includes the checks step (`hasRoomLocked`, `internal/daemon/runs.go:805`, adj 122); approve, answer and retry bypass the cap, and nothing makes a check wait for another run's check or for other work on the machine (landing alone has a lock, `internal/engine/landlock.go`). *Not verified:* what was running at the time and whether a timing test was the cause; the log says "likely" (F25). So this slice does not change admission; it adds the rerun, which is the cheap answer to a failure that load caused.

`checks.deterministic` (adj 31, decided) says ork runs the check command and `slicer check` after the implementer and red goes back without a review; a rerun keeps that rule. No slicer feature covers this (`slicer find rerun`, `slicer find flaky` list nothing relevant) and the check command is ork's to run (`docs/design.md:300-304`). `S234` and its discovered-from list name this friction as "check failures"; this is the slice.

Owner decisions (interactive question, 2026-11-02): the fix-round brief gets a Go-test-aware excerpt of at most 8000 bytes before the existing 30000-byte tail; the project check command is rerun once after an exit failure, not after a timeout and not for the slicer check; a pass on the rerun is recorded as flaky in `run.json` and the log only; making checks wait for other runs is not part of this slice.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
This slice touches `internal/engine` and `internal/runrec`: it is an E-class slice (at most one such slice per wave).

- `internal/engine/failures.go` (new): `FailureExcerpt(output string, limit int) (excerpt string, tests []string)`.
- `internal/engine/failures_test.go` (new).
- `internal/engine/check.go:19-34` (`RunCheck` sets `TimedOut`) and `internal/engine/engine.go:28-31` (`CheckOutput.TimedOut bool`).
- `internal/engine/states.go:110-111` (the `checks` brief) and `:268-327` (`runChecks`: one rerun, the log layout, the record fields). `noProgress` (`:136-153`) is read, not changed.
- `internal/engine/land.go:179` (the landing re-check brief uses the same helper).
- `internal/runrec/record.go:96-103` (`CheckRecord.Attempts`, `CheckRecord.Flaky`, both `omitempty`).
- `internal/engine/harness_test.go:127-146` (`fakeChecks` gets a per-call error switch and a `TimedOut` pass-through).
- Tests whose check-output sequences have a red entry (each red entry is now consumed twice, once by the rerun): `internal/engine/engine_test.go:301`, the S294 round-pause tests that use `redLoop` (from `:459`), `internal/engine/approval_test.go:554-555`, `internal/engine/architect_test.go:223`, and the `setCheckOutputs` calls at `internal/engine/land_test.go:370`, `:565`, `:621`, `:669`, `:933-935` and `:1005`. `internal/engine/recover_test.go:192` (`TestRunCheck` also checks `TimedOut`).
- `docs/design.md:300-304` (checks bullet) and `:540-543` (Checks), `docs/guide.md:258-259`, `docs/state.md:17`, `:232` and `:275-277` (the `checks[]` example, a sentence for `attempts` and `flaky`, and what `log_sha256` hashes when the log holds two runs).
- `CHANGELOG.md` (an entry under `## Unreleased`, marked *proposed*; add it last).

Pair planning: E-class. It must not share a wave with another E-class slice. S279 (round checks defer outside tracking problems) also edits `runChecks` and the check log, so the two must not share a wave; the second to land re-anchors on the first. It can pair with an N-class slice that leaves `docs/design.md` alone.

UI: none. `internal/tui`, `internal/cli` output and golden views are untouched; the flaky mark is in `run.json` and the log only.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
Write these first. Each fails today for the reason given (most first as a compile error: `FailureExcerpt`, `CheckOutput.TimedOut`, `CheckRecord.Attempts` do not exist).

`internal/engine/failures_test.go` (use go test text output copied in the test as a string):
- `TestFailureExcerptKeepsFailHeaderAndAssertionLines`: output with `ok` lines, then `--- FAIL: TestX (0.01s)`, `    x_test.go:12: got 1, want 2`, `FAIL`, `FAIL\tpkg\t0.5s`: the excerpt has the header, the assertion line and the `FAIL\tpkg` line, and `tests` is `["TestX"]`.
- `TestFailureExcerptSurvivesAnOutputLongerThanTheTail`: the failure comes first and 60 KB of other lines follow; `FailureExcerpt` still returns header and assertion, while `tail(output, 30000)` does not contain them (this is the F23 case).
- `TestFailureExcerptKeepsSubtestsAndTheirNames`: `--- FAIL: TestA (0.1s)` with an indented `    --- FAIL: TestA/sub (0.0s)` and its assertion; `tests` is `["TestA", "TestA/sub"]` in order, without repeats.
- `TestFailureExcerptKeepsPanicRaceAndBuildErrors`: a `panic: ` line with the next five lines; a `WARNING: DATA RACE` block up to its blank line (at most 25 lines); `# pkg` and `file.go:3:5: undefined: x` lines before `FAIL\tpkg [build failed]`.
- `TestFailureExcerptIsBounded`: 500 failing tests give at most `limit` bytes, whole lines only, and a last line `[N more failing tests not shown]` with the right N.
- `TestFailureExcerptCutsLongLinesOnARuneBoundary`: a 5000-byte assertion line is cut to 400 bytes plus `...` without splitting a UTF-8 rune.
- `TestFailureExcerptOfOtherOutputIsEmpty`: pytest-style output and plain `boom` give `""` and no tests, so the brief stays as it is today.

`internal/engine/engine_test.go` and `land_test.go` (new tests; the harness feeds `h.checks.outputs` one entry per call and repeats the last, `harness_test.go:134-146`):
- `TestRedCheckIsRunAgainOnceBeforeAFixRound`: outputs red then ok: no implementer fix round (roles `implementer-1`, `reviewer-1`, `gate-1`), the project command ran twice, `rec.Checks[0]` has `OK` true, `Attempts` 2, `Flaky` true, and `checks-1.log` holds both outputs in order with a heading that says the second is a rerun. Today: one call, a fix round.
- `TestCheckThatStaysRedSendsOneFixRoundWithTheFailures`: red, red: one fix round; the project command ran twice; `Attempts` 2, `Flaky` false; the brief has the failing test names and assertion lines of the second run ahead of the tail, and says the check failed twice.
- `TestFixBriefKeepsTheAssertionWhenTheOutputIsLong`: the red output has the failure first and 60 KB after it (twice); the brief contains the `--- FAIL` header and the assertion line. Today: they are cut.
- `TestFixBriefListsTestsThatFailedOnlyOnTheFirstRun`: first run fails `TestA` and `TestB`, second fails `TestB`: the brief names `TestA` under "failed on the first run only".
- `TestTimedOutCheckIsNotRunAgain`: a first result with `TimedOut` true: one call, then a fix round as today.
- `TestGreenCheckRunsOnce` and `TestRedSlicerCheckIsNotRunAgain`: the project command and `slicer check` each run once; only the project command is ever rerun.
- `TestRerunThatCannotRunPausesLikeTheFirstRun`: the second call returns an error: the run pauses with `check command: ` plus the error, kind `error`, state `checks`.
- `TestStalledRoundWithARerunStillPausesAtOnce`: two adjacent rounds with no tree change, each red on both runs with the same output: the run pauses at once with the no-progress reason (S294), because `log_sha256` of the two-run logs match. Guards the hash rule in Implement step 4.
- `TestLandRecheckIsRunAgainOnceToo`: after a merge-in the re-check is red, then ok: the landing continues without `landBlocked`, and `land-checks-1.log` holds both outputs.
- `TestLandRedRecheckBriefHasTheFailureExcerpt`: red, red after the merge: the `## Landing blocked` brief has the excerpt.
- `TestCheckRecordOmitsAttemptsAndFlakyWhenAbsent`: `run.json` of a first-time pass has neither key (older readers keep working).

`internal/engine/recover_test.go`:
- `TestRunCheck` (`:192`, extend): the timeout case has `TimedOut` true; a plain exit failure and a pass have it false.

Existing tests to change (they fail after the rerun is in, because a red entry is now consumed by the rerun): `TestRedChecksSendTheImplementerBackWithoutSpendingAReview` (`engine_test.go:301`: `red, red, ok`); the S294 tests built on `redLoop` (`engine_test.go:471`), among them `TestTheRoundLimitPausesARedLoop` (`:459`), `TestNoChangeAndTheSameCheckOutputPausesAtOnce` (`:609`) and `TestNoChangeButDifferentOutputDoesNotPauseEarly`, whose per-round outputs must now be given twice; the "red check" row in `approval_test.go:554-555`; `architect_test.go:223`; and the `setCheckOutputs` calls at `land_test.go:370`, `:565`, `:621`, `:669`, `:933-935` and `:1005`. Where the last output repeats, the test may pass unchanged; verify each.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
The steps follow the owner's answers of 2026-11-02 (see the Why section). Re-anchor every line number with `rg -n` first.

1. Tests first, in the order above. Run them and see each named failure.
2. `CheckOutput` gets `TimedOut bool`. `RunCheck` sets it in the `TimeoutError` branch only (`check.go:29-30`). Keep the existing output text.
3. `internal/engine/failures.go`, `FailureExcerpt(output, limit)`: go through the lines once. Keep (a) every line whose text after leading spaces starts `--- FAIL:`, with the lines under it that are indented deeper than it, at most 20 lines per test; (b) `FAIL` and `FAIL<TAB>` package lines; (c) a `panic: ` line and the five lines after it; (d) a `WARNING: DATA RACE` line and the lines after it up to a blank line, at most 25; (e) `# ` package lines and `FILE.go:N:N: message` lines. Cut a line to 400 bytes at a rune boundary and add `...`. Stop at `limit` bytes on a whole line and append `[N more failing tests not shown]`. Return the test names from the `--- FAIL:` lines in order, without repeats. Return `"", nil` when no `--- FAIL`, `panic:`, `DATA RACE` or build-error line was found. Use the standard library only. Go `-json` output is not parsed.
4. `internal/engine/states.go` `runChecks` (`:268`): after the first project-command run, when the result is not OK, `TimedOut` is false and the run was not cancelled, run the same command once more with the same directory and timeout. If the rerun cannot run, pause as the first run would. Write the log as the first run's `tail(output, 30000)` and, under a line `$ COMMAND (run again once: the first run failed)`, the second run's; then the `slicer check --json` part as today. Do not rerun `slicer check`. Set `ok` from the second result, and take `failure` (`checkFailureLine`) from the second result. Record `Attempts` 2, and `Flaky` true when the first failed and the second passed; `Seconds` stays the whole time of the step. A passing first run records neither field.
   - The log hash and the stall rule. *Proposed:* `LogSHA256` (`states.go:323`) keeps hashing the whole saved log, both project runs included, and `noProgress` (`:136-153`) is not changed. Two stalled rounds whose failure is deterministic write the same two outputs and the same slicer part, so their hashes still match and S294's immediate pause still fires. A round whose first run differs from its rerun (a flaky failure) will rarely match the next round's log, so that stall waits for the round-3 pause instead; this is the same as today for any output that varies between rounds. Do not hash only the second run: the log is what the owner and the fix round read, and `docs/state.md:275-277` says the hash is of the saved log bytes.
   - S279. If S279 (deferral of outside tracking problems, open) lands first, its `deferred to land (branch behind BASE): PROBLEM` lines stay after the slicer output, after both project runs; they are part of the saved log and so of the hash, as S279 writes them. The rerun touches only the project command, so S279's test of the slicer part is unchanged. If this slice lands first, S279 appends its lines after the slicer part of the two-run log.
5. The `checks` brief (`states.go:110-111`) and the landing brief (`land.go:179`): build the body with one helper, for example `checkFailureBody(log string) string`. When `FailureExcerpt(log, 8000)` is not empty the body is the line "The failing tests and assertion lines, cut to fit:", the excerpt in a fence, then "The end of the output:" and the existing `tail(log, 30000)` in a fence. When the log shows two runs, add one line that the check failed in both runs, and, if the first run's test names are not all in the second's, "Failed on the first run only: NAMES." When the excerpt is empty the body is what it is today.
6. `internal/runrec/record.go` (`CheckRecord`, `:96-103`): `Attempts int json:"attempts,omitempty"` and `Flaky bool json:"flaky,omitempty"`; no store version change (`omitempty` keys; older readers ignore them).
7. Docs: `docs/design.md:300-304` and `:540-543` (one rerun of the project command on an exit failure; the brief shows failing tests first), `docs/guide.md:258-259`, `docs/state.md` (the `checks[]` example at `:232`, one sentence for `attempts` and `flaky`, and at `:275-277` that `log_sha256` covers both runs). Mark the rerun and the excerpt *proposed*.
8. Do not touch: `internal/tui`, `internal/cli`, the admission code in `internal/daemon/runs.go`, the check timeout (`CheckMinutes`), `slicer check`, the round pause or `noProgress`, or any retry of a role.
9. Add the CHANGELOG entry last, as the first item under `## Unreleased`, marked *proposed*.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- `go test -race -count=1 ./...`; `go vet ./...`; `gofmt -l .`; `slicer check`; `adj lint`.
- `go test -race -count=1 -run 'FailureExcerpt|RedCheck|CheckThatStaysRed|FixBrief|TimedOutCheck|Recheck|RunCheck|CheckRecord|StalledRound|RoundLimit|NoChange|SameOutput' ./internal/engine`.
- `rg -n "slicer check" internal/engine/states.go` shows `slicer check` still runs once per step.
- [HUMAN CHECK] [AFTER LAND] In a scratch project whose check command fails the first time and passes the second (for example a script that touches a marker file), run one slice through ork: no fix round starts, and `checks-1.log` shows both runs. With a check that always fails, the fix round's brief starts with the failing test names.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: One commit on the slice branch: "Check failures: rerun a red check once and show the failing tests".
